    Pyrifos: Whole-Plot Random-Intercept PERMANOVA

    pyrifos-random-intercept.Rmd

    The vegan::pyrifos data contain aquatic invertebrate communities from 12 experimental ditches observed repeatedly. Insecticide dose was assigned to ditches, making a ditch the whole-plot and exchangeability unit for a dose test.

    data(pyrifos, package = "vegan")

ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = 132)
week <- factor(rep(c(-4, -1, 0.1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 15, 19, 24), each = 12))
dose <- factor(rep(c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6), 11))

# A balanced post-treatment window: four dates for every ditch.
keep <- week %in% c(1, 2, 4, 8)
pyrifos_post <- pyrifos[keep, ]
pyrifos_env <- data.frame(
  ditch = droplevels(ditch[keep]),
  week = droplevels(week[keep]),
  dose = droplevels(dose[keep])
)

with(pyrifos_env, table(ditch, week))
#>      week
#> ditch 1 2 4 8
#>    1  1 1 1 1
#>    2  1 1 1 1
#>    3  1 1 1 1
#>    4  1 1 1 1
#>    5  1 1 1 1
#>    6  1 1 1 1
#>    7  1 1 1 1
#>    8  1 1 1 1
#>    9  1 1 1 1
#>    10 1 1 1 1
#>    11 1 1 1 1
#>    12 1 1 1 1

    The response values supplied by vegan are already transformed. Here they are used to calculate Bray–Curtis dissimilarities.

    pyrifos_bray <- vegdist(pyrifos_post, method = "bray")
pyrifos_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ dose + (1 | ditch),
  data = pyrifos_env,
  distance = pyrifos_bray
)
pyrifos_design
#> Canonical PERMANOVA design
#> Observations: 48  Fixed rank: 5 
#> Fixed: dose 
#> Random: ditch 
#> Euclidean distance: FALSE 
#> Warnings: Dissimilarity is non-Euclidean; negative eigenvalues were retained.

    Dose is constant within each ditch and every ditch has four observations, so the balanced random-intercept engine can derive an exact EMS denominator.

    derive_ems(pyrifos_design)$dose
#> $term
#> [1] "dose"
#> 
#> $hypothesis
#> [1] "all estimable coefficients for `dose` are zero"
#> 
#> $numerator_df
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $numerator_under_null
#>         residual random_intercept 
#>                1                4 
#> 
#> $numerator_under_alternative
#>         residual random_intercept     fixed_effect 
#>                1                4                1 
#> 
#> $denominator
#>         residual random_intercept 
#>                1                4 
#> 
#> $denominator_term
#> [1] "ditch within fixed model"
#> 
#> $denominator_df
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $exact_denominator
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $derivation
#> [1] "Both numerator and denominator contain sigma[e]^2 + 4 sigma[ditch]^2 under H0; the fixed-effect component occurs only in the numerator under H1."
    pyrifos_fit <- permanova_mixed(
  pyrifos_design,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260718
)
pyrifos_fit
#> Distance-based balanced random-intercept model
#> Supported design: balanced single random intercept; fixed predictors constant within whole plots 
#> Permutation: term-specific Freedman-Lane whole-plot residual permutation 
#>                      term df        ss         ms                  denominator
#>                      dose  4 1.8946032 0.47365081 MS[ditch within fixed model]
#>  ditch within fixed model  7 0.9561482 0.13659260                         <NA>
#>              Within ditch 36 2.2378478 0.06216244                         <NA>
#>  denominator_df pseudo_f p_perm
#>               7 3.467617  0.005
#>              NA       NA     NA
#>              NA       NA     NA

    The test specification records the scientific and computational choices.

    with(pyrifos_fit$tests$dose, list(
  hypothesis = hypothesis,
  denominator = denominator$expression,
  exchangeable_units = exchangeable_units,
  permutation_algorithm = permutation_algorithm,
  attainable_permutations = attainable_permutations,
  approximation_status = approximation_status,
  warnings = warnings
))
#> $hypothesis
#> [1] "all estimable coefficients for `dose` are zero"
#> 
#> $denominator
#> [1] "MS[ditch within fixed model]"
#> 
#> $exchangeable_units
#> [1] "ditch"
#> 
#> $permutation_algorithm
#> [1] "Freedman-Lane residual permutation of whole plots"
#> 
#> $attainable_permutations
#> [1] 479001600
#> 
#> $approximation_status
#> [1] "Monte Carlo p-value"
#> 
#> $warnings
#> character(0)

    The whole-plot test addresses an average dose effect over the selected post-treatment dates. It does not estimate a dose-by-time response. A formula with week as a fixed effect varies within ditch and is outside the current random-intercept support envelope.

    time_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ week + (1 | ditch),
  data = pyrifos_env,
  distance = pyrifos_bray
)

tryCatch(
  permanova_mixed(time_design, permutations = 0),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
#> [1] "All fixed predictors must be constant within the random-intercept grouping units for the Phase 2 whole-plot test."

    That explicit failure prevents an invalid whole-plot permutation from being used for a within-ditch time hypothesis. A full longitudinal analysis would need a supported time covariance or random-slope structure.
